text:
taylor: Starting rollout v4.0.0 to dedicated pools (EU-E and US-E). Small canary to EU-E first. Heads up: change window open.

deploy-bot: Canary summary at 5%: instance_failure_rate 0.6% (threshold 0.8%), mem_rss_growth +18% in worker-1 over 10m. No auto-revert triggered.

nik: Saw a couple OOM restarts on EU-E worker-1. Traces point to long-lived KV cache objects in the new kernel change.

sylvia: Can we narrow to dedicated only? If this is kernel-related I'd prefer to stop the dedicated cutover and leave hosted flows intact.

linda-cs: Flagging CS and account owners for enterprise customers in EU/US that are on dedicated. Will prepare an advisory if we stop.

oncall-sre: If you want me to abort the dedicated rollout I can run the rollback command; confirm scope.

taylor: Do partial backout: set dedicated pools back to v3.9.9 and hold v4.0.0 in staging. Leave hosted API traffic moving. Suppress deploy-bot retries for rollout-id r-3298765400.

deploy-bot: Action: suppress-autoretry ON for rollout-id r-3298765400 (requested by taylor).

oncall-sre: Running: `rwctl rollout set --id r-3298765400 --scope dedicated --target v3.9.9 --percent 100`  — executing now.

nik: Rolling back dedicated looks clean so far. Restart counts decreasing. Mem growth stabilized on rolled-back hosts.

sylvia: Good. I'm going to pin EU-E/US-E dedicated pools to v3.9.9 for the rest of the window and add blocking flag so no auto-upgrades target them.

linda-cs: Drafted note to customers: "During a limited dedicated rollout to v4.0.0 we observed memory growth on some worker nodes. We have reverted dedicated clusters to v3.9.9 while we investigate. Hosted API unaffected." Posting to customer channel after legal review.

taylor: Adding action items: 1) open bug with traces + heap dumps (assign nik) 2) revert any config flips in kernel that touched kv cache (assign sylvia) 3) run extended soak on staging v4.0.0 with additional mem-profiling.

nik: Created ticket RI-2301 and attached sample heap dumps + small repro. Assigned to nik and sylvia.

oncall-sre: Monitoring rollback: instance_failure_rate down to 0.05% in 2m, restart_count trend flattening. p95 unaffected for hosted.

sylvia: I'll disable the new async-kv-prefetch flag at origin and push a canary build to staging with memory instrumentation.

taylor: Thanks. Keep the ping loop open for +90m. If anything spikes we re-open this thread and escalate to oncall-sre.

linda-cs: Customer advisory queued: link https://redwood.internal/advisories/3298765432. Sent to legal for signoff.

nik: One oddity: a single large tenant on US-E had higher allocation growth; including them in the dedicated-pin list so their SLA won't see the new version.

oncall-sre: Marking monitoring window until 329876... +90m. Will raise if metrics cross thresholds.

taylor: Closing the immediate rollback execution. Keep RD ticket RI-2301 updated with any new traces. We'll retest the v4 branch after kernel fix and memory soak.

linda-cs: Noted. I'll brief customer success and sales about the pinned pools and the next steps.

sylvia: Started a debug run in staging with `--mem-profile` and increased prefetch timeouts. Will post findings in RI-2301.

nik: Thanks everyone. :heart:
